Apache AGE + pgvector do NOT compose in a single graph+vector query (separate extensions); plan to orchestrate two queries, and note AGE's openCypher is less complete/tuned than Neo4j.

Confidence/version notes: Kuzu status, cosmos.gl MIT + v3.1 (June 2026), Graphiti bi-temporal model, AGE Apache-TLP/PG18, and DuckPGQ version pin were corroborated this session (high confidence). Exact FPS / node-ceiling numbers for Sigma/Cytoscape/cosmos.gl are workload-dependent vendor/benchmark claims — treat as order-of-magnitude only, which is precisely why the fixture experiment above is the real decider (medium confidence on the precise numbers).

result.domain: Observability, tracing & cost tracking for a swarm of hundreds of concurrent bounded agents (per-agent traces, token/cost, live run trees, self-hostable dashboard). Persona stack: lean stdlib backend, raw Anthropic SDK for the swarm, FastAPI + React UI already in place.

tools.name: OpenTelemetry GenAI + OpenInference instrumentation (openinference-instrumentation-anthropic)
tools.what: Vendor-neutral wire format + a monkey-patch instrumentor that emits per-call spans (prompts, responses, tool calls, token usage) for the Anthropic SDK over OTLP to ANY backend, and can also feed an in-process SpanProcessor.
tools.maturity: OTEL GenAI semconv still 'Development'/experimental as of Apr 2026 (attr names can drift), BUT core attrs (gen_ai.system, request.model, token counts) are stable and agent/workflow/tool/model spans are defined as of spec v1.41. OpenInference Anthropic + claude-agent-sdk instrumentors are shipping on PyPI. Confidence: high on the seam existing, medium on attr stability.
tools.why: This is the load-bearing choice: it is the seam, not a platform. One `pip install` + one `AnthropicInstrumentor().instrument()` gives per-agent spans with token usage, exportable to Phoenix OR Langfuse (swap backends behind the same exporter — insulates you from vendor churn). Critically, the SAME spans can be tapped by a custom in-process OTEL SpanProcessor that pushes compact events into your existing FastAPI SSE/WebSocket for the live control room. One instrumentation, two sinks (durable backend + live UI). Nothing else here gives you that decoupling.
tools.integration_cost: Low. ~15 lines in the swarm entrypoint. Gotcha: instrumentor must run BEFORE `import anthropic` or spans silently vanish — assert-at-startup. Pin versions and set OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental for dual-emit; keep an attr-name mapping layer so a semconv rename doesn't break your SpanProcessor.

tools.name: Arize Phoenix (self-host)
tools.what: Single-container, OTEL/OpenInference-native trace store + waterfall/run-tree UI + eval. localhost:6006. No event caps self-hosted.
tools.maturity: Mature, actively developed. Elastic License 2.0 (source-available, not OSI-approved — fine for internal/research use; only matters if you'd redistribute). Default SQLite, optional Postgres. Confidence: high.
tools.why: Best fit for the DURABLE per-agent trace/debug/forensics surface IF you decide you need one beyond Persona's own notebook log. Lightest self-host that holds: one `docker run`, no ClickHouse/Redis/S3 to babysit, no per-trace cost. OpenInference-native so it consumes your instrumentation with zero glue. Use it for the engineer-facing 'replay this agent's run' tab — NOT as your live control room (see recommendation).
tools.integration_cost: Low. `docker run` + point the OTLP exporter at :6006. Caveat: single-process + SQLite/Postgres may bottleneck at sustained hundreds-of-agents x high-QPS — validate at target concurrency before trusting it for the demo money-shot; that stress signal is exactly what tells you whether you need the heavier Langfuse tier.

tools.name: Langfuse (self-host, OSS)
tools.what: MIT-core LLM observability platform: nested traces, token/cost with built-in Anthropic price tables, filter by session/cost/latency/metadata, OTLP ingestion, plus prompt-mgmt/evals/datasets/LLM-as-judge. ClickHouse-backed OLAP.
tools.maturity: Very mature; acquired by ClickHouse Jan 2026 (healthy for longevity + scale, roadmap now steered by acquirer). MIT core is genuinely open + uncapped when self-hosted. Confidence: high.
tools.why: Technically excellent and the right answer at SCALE (ClickHouse handles high sustained trace volume that Phoenix's single process may not). Two conditions gate it: (1) you actually need historical trace analytics at volume, not just the live stream + notebook — otherwise it is heavier than the need; (2) DISCIPLINE — its prompt-mgmt/evals/scores/datasets DIRECTLY DUPLICATE Persona's belief-store/membrane/engine. Adopting those creates a second, competing source of truth about 'what Persona believes.' Use it as a trace store ONLY, or don't use it.
tools.integration_cost: SDK/OTLP side: low. Infra side: medium-heavy — Postgres + ClickHouse + Redis/Valkey + S3 + 2 app containers, ~4 CPU/16GB/100GB floor for prod. That's real ops surface for a research project; it earns its place only past Phoenix's ceiling.

tools.name: Helicone (self-host)
tools.what: Apache-2.0 proxy-first gateway + observability: every LLM call routes THROUGH its proxy, which logs req/resp, token/cost (300+ model price DB), caching, rate limits. Anthropic gateway supported self-hosted.
tools.maturity: Acquired by Mintlify Mar 2026, now in MAINTENANCE MODE. Repo/Docker still current but no active roadmap. Confidence: high on the acquisition/maintenance status.
tools.why: Three strikes for Persona: (1) maintenance mode — do not build a NEW prod dependency on it; (2) the proxy model inserts a network hop + single point of failure in front of EVERY one of hundreds of concurrent agent calls, and you surrender the direct Anthropic streaming/retry/timeout control you own in-process; (3) you already get exact token/cost from the Anthropic response `usage` field for free — a ~20-line price dict beats standing up a proxy for the one thing it'd buy you.
tools.integration_cost: Deceptively low (one base-URL swap) but the wrong axis — the cost is architectural: a proxy SPOF and lost in-process call control, for a capability you already have from the SDK.

tools.name: LangSmith (self-host)
tools.what: LangChain's agent/LLM observability platform. Purpose-built agent trace store (SmithDB), deep nested run trees, evals.
tools.maturity: Mature, commercial, closed. Self-host is an Enterprise-only add-on (Kubernetes, BYOC/self-host). Third-party estimates put the Enterprise floor around ~$100K/yr (unofficial figure — treat as directional). Confidence: high on 'enterprise-only self-host', medium on the exact dollar figure.
tools.why: Fails the two hard constraints. Self-host is gated behind a heavy Enterprise commitment — a non-starter for this project's scale. Cloud free tier (5K traces/mo) is blown apart instantly by hundreds of agents AND ships your traces off-infra. Also LangChain-centric while Persona uses the raw Anthropic SDK — no leverage from its ecosystem. Nothing here that Phoenix/Langfuse don't give self-hosted for free.
tools.integration_cost: N/A — blocked by licensing/cost before integration is even relevant.

tools.name: Pydantic Logfire (honorable-mention, not in original list)
tools.what: OTEL-native full-stack observability from the Pydantic team; one-line FastAPI instrument, native Pydantic-AI integration, LLM/agent tracing.
tools.maturity: Mature, best-in-class DX for a Pydantic/FastAPI shop (which Persona is). Confidence: high.
tools.why: Surfaced because Persona is exactly its sweet spot (FastAPI + Pydantic), so honest scouting must name it — but the backend is CLOSED and self-host is Enterprise-only, which fails Persona's self-hostable requirement. If cloud-with-data-leaving were ever acceptable it'd be the nicest DX of the lot; under the self-host constraint it's out. Because everything rides OTLP, you could still swap it in later behind the same exporter with zero rework.
tools.integration_cost: Low DX, but blocked by the self-host constraint — same OTLP seam means switching later is cheap if the constraint changes.

result.recommendation: Separate the two needs people conflate. (A) The LIVE 'swarm control room' — hundreds of agents in flight, membrane admit/reject, belief updates — is Persona's PRODUCT and its legibility thesis; NO off-the-shelf tool gives it to you (every one here is an engineer's trace explorer, not an editorial 'mind at work' view). Build it yourself in the existing React UI. (B) The durable per-agent trace/forensics backend is undifferentiated plumbing you should NOT hand-roll. Bridge both with ONE instrumentation: instrument the swarm's Anthropic SDK once with OpenInference (OTLP), then fan to two sinks — (1) a custom in-process OTEL SpanProcessor that pushes compact per-agent events over your existing FastAPI SSE/WebSocket into the React control room, and (2) a self-hosted Arize Phoenix container as the debug/replay backend. Get live token/cost straight from the Anthropic `usage` field x a ~20-line price dict — don't stand up Helicone's proxy for it. Adopt Langfuse instead of Phoenix ONLY when you outgrow Phoenix's single-process ceiling AND accept the ClickHouse infra, and even then restrict it to trace storage so it never becomes a second brain competing with the belief-store. Skip LangSmith (Enterprise-only self-host) and Helicone (maintenance mode + proxy SPOF). Net: raw Anthropic SDK + OpenInference seam + your own SSE control room + Phoenix as the debug tab — a framework earns its place only at the trace-store rung, and only Phoenix/Langfuse clear the self-host bar there.
result.discriminating_experiment: Spin up Phoenix (single `docker run`) and run ONE swarm burst of ~50 concurrent agents instrumented with openinference-instrumentation-anthropic exporting OTLP. Measure three things: (a) does Phoenix render the per-agent run tree + token/cost at 50-concurrency without dropping spans; (b) the added p50/p95 latency and CPU from instrumentation on your agent calls; (c) can a custom SpanProcessor tap the same spans and push to your SSE hub in <200ms end-to-end. Decision rule: if the SpanProcessor->SSE path is clean, you've proven the 'one instrumentation, two sinks' architecture AND you may not even need the heavy backend for the live view. If Phoenix drops spans or the run-tree is unusable at 50 agents, that's your explicit signal to move the trace-store sink up to the Langfuse/ClickHouse tier — without touching the instrumentation or the live UI, because both sit behind the OTLP seam.
risks: Semconv instability: OTEL GenAI conventions are still 'Development' as of Apr 2026 — attribute names can change without a major bump. Pin instrumentation versions, set OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental for dual-emit, and keep an attr-name mapping layer so a rename doesn't silently break the live SpanProcessor.

Duplication trap (the real DPI-style risk here): Langfuse/LangSmith ship prompt-mgmt, evals, scores and datasets that OVERLAP Persona's belief-store/membrane/engine. Adopting those features creates a second, conflicting source of truth about 'what Persona believes.' If you adopt Langfuse, restrict it to trace storage only.

The live control room is NOT free from any tool: budget to build it in React. The observability backends only back the forensics/debug tab; presenting an inferred belief or a mid-flight agent with the same visual authority as a confirmed one would violate Persona's honest-uncertainty principle — a generic trace UI won't respect that, your own UI must.

Phoenix single-process + SQLite/Postgres may bottleneck at sustained hundreds-of-agents x high-QPS. Validate at target concurrency before the demo, and per Persona's caching principle, cache/replay pre-run traces so nothing live can break the money-shot.

Vendor churn is live in this space: Helicone->Mintlify (maintenance, Mar 2026), Langfuse->ClickHouse (acquired Jan 2026). Betting on the OTLP wire format rather than any one vendor's proprietary SDK is what keeps Phoenix<->Langfuse<->Logfire swappable — treat that seam as the durable choice, the backend as replaceable.

Instrumentation ordering: AnthropicInstrumentor().instrument() must run before `import anthropic` or spans vanish silently — a silent-wrong-observability bug is exactly the fail-loud boundary Persona's principles call out. Assert instrumentation is active at startup.
Don't run BOTH Phoenix and Langfuse — pick one backend behind the OTLP exporter; two trace stores is duplicated ops for no gain.

Citation confidence: tool existence/architecture claims are high-confidence (official docs/PyPI/GitHub). The LangSmith '~$100K/yr' self-host floor is a third-party estimate (unofficial) — directional only. Acquisition dates (Helicone/Mintlify Mar 2026, Langfuse/ClickHouse Jan 2026) come from secondary sources; verify against the vendors' own announcements before quoting.

result.domain: State-of-the-art many-agent / deep-research systems for biomedical literature analysis (2025-2026)

tools.name: Anthropic orchestrator-worker research pattern (the pattern, not a product)
tools.what: Lead agent plans and decomposes a breadth-first query, spawns 3-5 parallel subagents each with its own context window and one bounded objective, then a separate pass synthesizes and attaches citations. Shipped as Claude Research (Apr 2025).
tools.maturity: Mature, production-proven pattern; high confidence on the numbers (from Anthropic's own engineering post).
tools.why: This is exactly Persona's swarm architecture already: self/engine = lead, ephemeral bounded readers = subagents, separate citation pass = provenance layer. Anthropic's own data VALIDATES Persona's split: multi-agent beat single-agent Opus by 90.2% ONLY on breadth-first parallel-reading tasks, and they explicitly say it FAILS on 'tasks that require all agents to share context or have many dependencies' and that 'LLM agents are not yet great at coordinating in real time.' That is the same boundary as Persona's DPI finding - parallelize independent READING (map), never parallelize interdependent REASONING (debate). Adopt it as a prompt-engineering playbook, not a dependency: teach the orchestrator to hand each reader an objective + boundaries + output format + tool guidance (their headline lesson - vague 'research X' caused subagents to duplicate the 2021 chip crisis while others redid 2025 supply chains).
tools.integration_cost: Low - it is a pattern Persona already implements; the value is the delegation-prompt discipline and the 'scale reads with more agents / scale reasoning by not adding agents' rule.

tools.name: PaperQA2 (Future-House/paper-qa)
tools.what: Apache-2.0 domain-specialized agentic-RAG library for scientific literature: three-phase pipeline (LLM keyword search -> vector + LLM re-ranking with contextual summarization 'RCS' -> grounded answer), citation-graph traversal, Semantic Scholar / Crossref / Unpaywall / OpenAlex / clinical-trials sources, local PDF corpus via tantivy, LiteLLM (any model incl. local). `pip install paper-qa>=5`, Python 3.11+.
tools.maturity: Mature, active OSS (v5+). Benchmark claims ('superhuman', SOTA on RAG-QA Arena science, tops LitQA2) are real but from the authors on their own MCQ-biology benchmark - treat 'superhuman' as narrow, medium confidence.
tools.why: The ONE framework here that earns its place, because it is NOT a generic many-agent orchestrator - it is a purpose-built reader+evidence-gatherer with citation traversal and contradiction detection, i.e. the exact 'scale of reading' muscle Persona's swarm needs, already benchmarked and provenance-friendly. Conditional, not blind ADOPT, because: (1) its built-in contradiction detection OVERLAPS Persona's membrane/belief-store - scope it to reader-only or you create two sources of truth; keep Persona as the arbiter of believing; (2) 'superhuman' is LitQA2 MCQ from the same lab, so per CLAUDE.md do not design around the claim without your own eval; (3) RCS reranking is compute-heavy - caching is mandatory. Use it to REPLACE hand-rolled read+extract in the swarm, not the self or the membrane.
tools.integration_cost: Medium - pip install, point its retriever at your cached Europe PMC corpus, wire LiteLLM to your model; the harder cost is drawing the line so it feeds evidence INTO the membrane rather than deciding truth itself.

tools.name: STORM / Co-STORM (stanford-oval, DSPy)
tools.what: Two-stage report generator: discovers multiple perspectives on a topic, simulates perspective-driven writer<->expert Q&A grounded on sources to build a citation graph and outline, then writes a Wikipedia-style report. Co-STORM adds a human-in-the-loop shared 'mind map' and collaborative discourse.
tools.maturity: Mature research code, widely used, DSPy-based. High confidence it works; well-known weakness: outputs are broad-but-shallow, neutrality/coverage over depth.
tools.why: Mine the MECHANISM, do not adopt the package. Two ideas are directly useful to Persona: (a) perspective-driven question generation to drive what the swarm reads (better coverage than a single query expansion), and (b) the grounded citation-graph outline, which maps onto Persona's dependency-graph 'what does the field rest on' screen. Co-STORM's human-steered mind map aligns with Persona's human-as-resolver + legibility ethos. But the deliverable (a neutral Wikipedia article) is the opposite of Persona's goal (an opinionated, evolving, falsifiable belief-state), and adopting it means a DSPy buy-in on top of your lean stdlib backend. Re-implement the two mechanisms in ~tens of lines; skip the framework.
tools.integration_cost: Low if you copy the mechanism; Medium-High if you adopt STORM+DSPy wholesale (new framework, compilation model, and an output format you would fight).

tools.name: Google DeepMind AI co-scientist (Gemini 2.0)
tools.what: Many-agent 'generate -> debate -> rank (Elo tournament) -> evolve' loop for hypothesis generation, with asynchronous task execution and test-time-compute scaling. Reported wet-lab-confirmed wins (AML drug repurposing, liver-fibrosis epigenetic targets).
tools.maturity: Research prototype, closed (not released, Gemini-only). Low external confidence: wet-lab 'validations' are a handful of anecdotes from the authors, not independently replicated; expert-novelty ratings are on 15 goals.
tools.why: Overlaps Persona's intellectual engine (contradiction -> hypothesis -> value queue). Steal ONE idea: rank candidate hypotheses by an Elo/tournament so the value queue surfaces the highest-leverage experiment - a clean, cheap addition. But the many-agent debate machinery is precisely what Persona's DPI finding and the MAST taxonomy warn against: it is the ~10x-cost, low-marginal-gain pattern. And it is closed, so nothing here is directly integratable. Adopt the tournament-ranking concept; skip the agent swarm-of-critics implementation. Rate the celebrated results with skepticism - they are cherry-picked and unreplicated.
tools.integration_cost: Idea-only: Low (a scoring/ranking function over the hypothesis queue). Full system: N/A (not released).

tools.name: Agentic RAG patterns (single-agent reflection/tool-use vs multi-agent) - the design space, per 2025 surveys
tools.what: Taxonomy of retrieval patterns: single-agent + tool-use, self-correcting/reflective RAG, corrective/adaptive/graph RAG, and multi-agent-with-specialized-retrievers. Surveys note multi-agent collaboration is 'less predictable' than reflection/tool-use, and agentic RAG costs 2-5x the LLM calls of static RAG.
tools.maturity: Well-established patterns; survey-level synthesis, high confidence on the qualitative guidance.
tools.why: This reinforces Persona's lean bet with independent evidence: reflection + tool-use + self-correction on a SINGLE strong agent are the mature, reliable patterns, while multi-agent collaboration is the unpredictable one. 67% of enterprise RAG deployments reportedly failed accuracy bars on complex queries, and cost is 2-5x - so the right move is a strong single reader with iterative query expansion and a verification/reflection step (which PaperQA2 already embodies) rather than more agents. Use the corrective/self-check pattern as the guard before anything writes into the belief-state.
tools.integration_cost: Low - these are patterns you fold into the existing read/verify loop, not a dependency.

tools.name: Open deep-research clones (LangChain open_deep_research / LangGraph, HuggingFace smolagents)
tools.what: OSS reimplementations of Deep Research. LangChain: LangGraph supervisor-researcher graph, section-by-section parallel plan (RACE ~0.43). smolagents: 'code agents' that act by writing Python; open_deep_research hits ~55% GAIA vs OpenAI's 67%.
tools.maturity: Active but churny (LangGraph especially); framework-heavy. Medium confidence, moving targets.
tools.why: Persona already has a working lean orchestrator; adopting LangGraph/LangChain means an abstraction tax and dependency churn to buy a supervisor-researcher graph you already have, and it re-imports the generic multi-agent overhead your DPI finding rejected. One exception worth cherry-picking (not adopting): smolagents' code-as-action pattern is a good fit for Persona's 'first-pass reanalysis' step where an agent must write and run analysis code on a located dataset - lift that idea, not the framework. Do not rip out a working backend to sit on someone else's graph engine.
tools.integration_cost: High to adopt (framework migration + lock-in); Low to borrow the smolagents code-agent idea for the reanalysis loop only.

tools.name: GPT-Researcher (assafelovic, planner-executor-publisher)
tools.what: Popular (~28k star) autonomous web-research agent: planner generates questions, parallel executors gather, publisher writes a report. Any-LLM.
tools.maturity: Mature OSS, but generic web research; documented hallucination and shallow/biased-source failure modes.
tools.why: Redundant with Persona's loop (planner-executor already exists) and worse for the domain: it optimizes for a polished web-sourced report, not a provenance-typed, contradiction-driven belief-state, and it lacks scientific-source specialization and citation verification. Its own listed failure modes (hallucination, selective/biased web sources) are exactly what would poison Persona's belief-store. Nothing here beats PaperQA2 for scientific reading or Persona's own engine for the acting loop.
tools.integration_cost: N/A - not worth integrating.

tools.name: Hosted Deep Research products (OpenAI Deep Research, Gemini/Google Deep Research)
tools.what: Closed, hosted deep-research agents that browse and produce cited long-form reports. State of the art on GAIA-style browsing.
tools.maturity: Mature products; closed weights/orchestration, no self-hosting, no belief-state hooks.
tools.why: Not integratable as infrastructure: you cannot host them, cannot control provenance typing, cannot let Persona's membrane arbitrate, and cannot cache their internals for a reproducible demo. Value is purely as a UX/quality BENCHMARK - a bar to beat on 'reads at scale, cites correctly' and a reference for the report-legibility UI, nothing to build on.
tools.integration_cost: N/A - reference/benchmark only.

result.recommendation: Keep Persona's lean stdlib orchestrator as-is: it already IS the Anthropic orchestrator-worker pattern (self/engine = lead, disposable swarm = parallel readers, provenance layer = citation pass), which the evidence validates specifically for breadth-first reading and warns against for interdependent reasoning - matching Persona's own DPI finding. Do NOT adopt LangGraph/LangChain, DSPy, GPT-Researcher, or any many-agent debate/consensus stack; MAST's 14 failure modes + the 15x token cost + your DPI result all say more agents != better. Make exactly ONE framework adoption: PaperQA2 (Apache-2.0) as the swarm's read/evidence primitive (citation-traversal RAG over your cached Europe PMC/OpenAlex corpus), while keeping Persona's membrane and belief-store as the sole arbiter of what to believe - scale-of-reading from PaperQA2, discipline-of-believing stays yours. Then hand-roll two small mechanisms internally (~tens of lines each, no new deps): STORM's perspective-driven question generation to broaden what the swarm reads, and the AI co-scientist Elo/tournament to rank hypotheses in the value queue. Net stack: raw Anthropic SDK + your purpose-built orchestrator + PaperQA2 as the reader + two borrowed mechanisms. That gives you the cutting edge where it pays (domain-specialized reading, calibrated hypothesis ranking) without importing the many-agent overhead you already proved is a loss.
result.discriminating_experiment: Three-arm reader bake-off over one fixed corpus. Take ~25-30 biomedical claims with known ground-truth support/contradiction (LitQA2-style, or hand-seed from your Europe PMC cache), freeze the corpus, and run: (A) Persona's current lean swarm reader; (B) PaperQA2 pointed at the same corpus; (C) a single strong Claude agent with tool-use + a reflection/self-check pass (the agentic-RAG 'mature pattern' baseline). Seed everything, >=20 runs, report mean +/- 95% CI on three metrics: grounded-answer accuracy (correct support vs contradiction), hallucinated-citation rate (cited span actually exists and says what is claimed), and tokens/$ per claim. Decision rule stated up front: adopt PaperQA2 only if it beats BOTH baselines on grounding accuracy AND hallucinated-cite rate by a margin that justifies its higher call-count; if the single-agent+reflection arm (C) matches it, keep lean and just add the reflection guard. This one experiment discriminates 'adopt PaperQA2' vs 'keep lean' and re-tests the DPI finding on the actual reading task instead of trusting anyone's benchmark.
risks: Framework lock-in / abstraction tax: adopting LangGraph/DSPy/smolagents bolts a heavy, churny dependency onto a working lean backend and is expensive to reverse; the borrowed-mechanism route avoids this but requires the discipline to NOT import the whole framework 'for convenience'.

Two-sources-of-truth: PaperQA2 ships its own contradiction detection that overlaps Persona's membrane/belief-store. If not scoped to reader-only, you get double-counting and ambiguous arbitration. Contract it as an evidence-gatherer that feeds the membrane; the membrane stays the sole judge.

Believing claimed SOTA without your own eval (violates CLAUDE.md 'never assume SOTA'): 'superhuman' PaperQA2 is narrow MCQ biology from the authors' own LitQA2; the co-scientist wet-lab wins are a handful of unreplicated anecdotes. Run the discriminating experiment before designing around either.

Re-importing many-agent overhead: copying Deep Research clones or the co-scientist swarm wholesale re-introduces the exact ~10x-cost / low-gain pattern your DPI finding and MAST (14 failure modes: role drift, step repetition, unverified outputs) already reject. Add agents only to parallelize independent READS, never interdependent reasoning.

Citation/tool-output hallucination poisoning the belief-state: deep-research agents hallucinate citations and even imagine tool outputs (EnIGMA failure mode). A silent wrong number written as a belief is the worst bug in this system - a hard citation-verification gate (span exists AND supports the claim) must sit before any READ->belief promotion.

Cost/latency of reading at scale: agentic RAG is 2-5x the LLM calls of static RAG and PaperQA2's RCS reranking is compute-heavy. Without the aggressive caching already in Persona's plan, the economics and the live demo both break - pre-cache Europe PMC/OpenAlex lookups and any reranking results.
